Earnings Call Transcript
YETI (YETI) Q4 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Updated Feb 19, 2026 at 10:48AM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


Date
Feb. 19, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. ET
Call participants
President and Chief Executive Officer — Matthew J. Reintjes
Chief Financial Officer — Michael James McMullen
Head of Investor Relations — Arvind Bhatia
Takeaways
Net sales
-- $583.7 million, marking 5% year-over-year growth and the strongest quarter of the year.
Drinkware sales
-- $380 million, up 6% globally; flat in the US due to promotional activity and wholesale caution.
Coolers and equipment sales
-- $192 million, up 2%, with soft coolers, bags, and cargo showing continued strength; hard coolers held stable despite lapping a 17% growth comp.
Direct-to-consumer sales
-- $394 million, up 5%, with broad-based growth across Amazon Marketplace, corporate sales, retail stores, and YETI-owned e-commerce.
Wholesale sales
-- $189 million, up 6%, driven by exceptional international results and supported by reduced US partner inventory levels.
International sales
-- $136 million, up 25%, now 23% of quarterly sales versus 20% prior; Europe and Australia highlighted for exceptional channel and category performance.
Adjusted gross profit
-- $341 million, representing 58.4% of sales, down 180 basis points, with a 310 basis point headwind from tariffs partially offset by lower product costs and select price increases.
Adjusted SG&A
-- $246 million, up 10%, with SG&A rising 190 basis points to 42.2% of sales due to growth investments, offset by distribution and fulfillment leverage.
Adjusted operating income
-- $94.7 million, down 14%, at a margin of 16.2%, with approximately 250 basis point net tariff impact.
Adjusted net income
-- $71.8 million, down 15%, at 12.3% of sales; adjusted EPS declined to $0.92 from $1.00, including a $0.15 tariff impact.
Free cash flow
-- $212 million for the year, exceeding adjusted net income and demonstrating strong operational cash generation.
Share repurchase
-- $125 million repurchased in the quarter (3.1 million shares), totaling $298 million for 2025 (8.2 million shares); 14% total share reduction over two years.
Cash position
-- $188 million at quarter-end, down from $359 million year prior, with total debt at $74 million.
2026 net sales growth guidance
-- 6%-8% expected, with Coolers & Equipment forecast at high single digit to low double digit % and Drinkware at mid-single digit %; international growth guided at high teens to 20%.
2026 gross margin guidance
-- 56%-57%; midpoint down 90 basis points year over year, with ~200 basis point incremental tariff headwind embedded, concentrated in the first half.
2026 adjusted operating income margin guidance
-- Approximately 14.4%, unchanged year over year, with margin declines expected in first half but offset by second-half expansion.
2026 adjusted EPS guidance
-- $2.77 to $2.83, representing 12%-14% growth, including an incremental $0.35 per share tariff headwind versus 2025.
2026 free cash flow guidance
-- $200 million to $225 million anticipated, marking a fourth consecutive year exceeding $200 million; $60 million to $70 million capex guided, focused on supply chain, technology, and innovation.
Supply chain update
-- China exposure reduced through geographic diversification; optimization, cost focus, and new factory ramp cited, with innovation centers and automation investments increasing flexibility and productivity.
Leadership transition
-- Scott Bomar appointed CFO, beginning Feb. 23, as Michael James McMullen transitions to an advisory role until May 31; management cited continuity and experience in financial discipline and operational scale.

Risks
Adjusted gross margin fell 180 basis points due to a 310 basis point tariff headwind, with guidance for further impact from tariffs in the first half of 2026.
Adjusted operating income declined 14% and adjusted net income declined 15%, with management citing tariffs and SG&A deleverage as main contributors.
US wholesale partners maintained buying caution, resulting in continued reduction of YETI inventory levels within the channel.
First half 2026 operating margin expected to decline by approximately 500 basis points, driven by the timing of tariff impacts, brand marketing spend, and incentive compensation accruals.
Summary
YETI Holdings

(
YETI

2.98%
)
reported its strongest quarterly net sales and international growth of the year, underscoring resilience across core and expanding categories. The company’s full-year free cash flow exceeded adjusted net income, supporting a $125 million share repurchase in the quarter and a total annual program of $298 million. Management guided 2026 net sales growth at 6%-8%, with pronounced strength forecast internationally, but noted headwinds from tariffs will weigh most heavily in the first half, driving year-over-year declines in gross and operating margin before anticipated improvements in the latter half. Strategic focus for 2026 includes accelerated product innovation, geographic expansion, and operational leverage, as outlined by the newly announced incoming CFO as part of a broader leadership transition.
Management expects 2026 adjusted operating income margin to remain flat at approximately 14.4%, with back-half recovery offsetting first-half pressure from tariffs and SG&A timing.
Tariffs will add roughly $80 million in 2026 cost of goods sold, with the majority related to AIPA tariffs, and management assumes no near-term relief within guidance.
International now represents 21% of sales, up from 2% at IPO, and is expected to remain a primary growth driver given ongoing investments in distribution, localized marketing, and omnichannel model expansion.
In response to promotional pressure and evolving consumer behavior, YETI continues to diversify its Drinkware offerings and expand shelf presence, while monitoring wholesale de-stocking and channel inventory tightly.
Industry glossary
DTC (Direct-to-consumer)
: Sales through company-owned e-commerce, retail, and digital channels, bypassing third-party retailers.
AIPA (Assessment and Investigation of Potential Additional Duties)
: Refers to a set of US import tariffs, including those contested or under legal review, affecting cost of goods imported from certain countries.
Sell-in / Sell-through
: Sell-in refers to sales from YETI to distributors or retailers; sell-through tracks sales from those partners to end consumers.
SG&A (Selling, general, and administrative expenses)
: Non-production operating expenses, including marketing, personnel, and administrative costs.
Camino, DayTrip, GoBox, Roadie, Scala
: Product families within YETI’s Coolers & Equipment and bags portfolio, each targeting specific outdoor, storage, or recreational use cases.

This headwind is on top of the 230 basis point gross tariff impact in 2025, which was concentrated in the back half of last year. Given these dynamics, from a phasing standpoint, we expect year-over-year gross margins to be down approximately 300 basis points in the first half of the year, with the year-over-year decline greater in Q1.
As we lap the full impact of tariffs in 2026, we expect second half gross margins to expand year over year as compared to 2025. In terms of OpEx, we expect full year growth of between 3% to 7% versus 2025, reflecting operating leverage and cost discipline. From a phasing perspective, we expect higher OpEx growth in the first half of the year versus the back half of the year. More specifically, we expect approximately 200 basis points of deleverage in the first half. There are two discrete items that are driving this dynamic.
First, our brand marketing spend will shift earlier in the year with the next phase of our campaign launching in the first half of 2026 versus a second half launch in 2025. Second, incentive compensation will return to a more consistent accrual pattern in 2026. In 2025, our incentive compensation accruals were reduced midyear following tariff announcements.
We expect 2026 adjusted operating income margin to be approximately 14.4%, consistent with 2025, leading to adjusted operating income growth of 6% to 8% for the full year, driven by the timing dynamics in gross margin and operating expenses that I just mentioned, which again are the unfavorable year-over-year impact of tariffs in the first half of the year and the timing shift of brand marketing and incentive compensation from the second half into the first half of the year. We expect first half operating margins to decline approximately 500 basis points, but we expect this to be fully offset by an approximately 400 basis points increase in the second half, resulting in flat operating margins for the year.
Before we move down the rest of the P&L, I wanted to take a minute to comment on our gross margins and operating expenses in 2025 and 2026 and then provide some thoughts on the opportunities in these line items beyond 2026. In 2026, tariffs will add roughly $80,000,000 to our cost of goods relative to 2024. That represents approximately 430 basis points of impact on our gross margins. Yet the midpoint of our 2026 gross margin guide, 56.5%, would imply only a 210 basis point decline over that same period. The difference represents our efforts to drive cost improvements and take pricing actions, which are helping to offset the impact of tariffs.
As we move into the second half of 2026 and fully lap tariffs, we expect those actions to drive year-over-year gross margin improvement with continued opportunity beyond 2026. As for operating expenses, we have made targeted investments over the past several years to support product innovation, international expansion, and global brand growth. As these initiatives scale in 2026, we expect to begin realizing operating expense leverage and we expect that to continue beyond 2026 as well. In terms of the remaining P&L items in our guide, we expect an effective tax rate this year of approximately 24%. We expect full year 2026 diluted shares outstanding of approximately 76,600,000 compared to 81,600,000 in 2025.
This reflects the full year impact of $298,000,000 in share repurchases during 2025 as well as an additional $100,000,000 in share repurchases planned for 2026. We expect adjusted earnings per diluted share of between $2.77 and $2.83 in 2026, reflecting growth of 12% to 14%. Our 2026 guidance includes an incremental $0.35 net unfavorable impact from higher tariff costs versus 2025. Capital expenditures are expected to be between $60,000,000 and $70,000,000 for the full year. Our capital spending remains focused on advancing our technology, launching innovative products, and strengthening our supply chain. We expect free cash flow of between $200,000,000 and $225,000,000 in 2026, which will be our fourth consecutive year of over $200,000,000 in free cash flow.
Note that our planned share repurchases in 2026 of $100,000,000 represent approximately 50% of our free cash flow this year. We are proud of the strong finish to 2025 and the momentum we are carrying into the year ahead. Our performance reflects not only the strength of the brand, but the operational discipline and strategic execution of our teams around the world. With that, I will turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.
